description:
This theme brings together research that has advanced the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care of cancer across a range of major cancer types, including prostate, breast, ovarian, and colorectal cancers. A core focus lies in developing and implementing targeted therapies, precision medicine, and patient-centred treatment strategies that improve survival rates, reduce side effects, and enhance quality of life for cancer patients.

Studies in this theme frequently contribute to the design and optimisation of screening and early detection programmes, improved imaging and diagnostic technologies, and innovations in radiotherapy, surgery, and pharmaceutical treatment. Many case studies address evidence-based clinical decision-making, guideline development, and updates to national and international standards of care.

Patient experience and supportive care are central concerns throughout, including efforts to enhance communication, reduce disparities in access to care, and improve post-treatment outcomes. The theme also captures the integration of clinical trials into practice, and the role of cancer research in shaping health services, public health initiatives, and policy development.

Overall, this theme reflects a broad and applied body of research that spans laboratory science, clinical practice, healthcare systems, and patient advocacy—focused on delivering better outcomes across the cancer care pathway.

This theme brings together research that enhances health, wellbeing, and care across a wide range of medical conditions, population groups, and health system contexts. It includes advances in diagnostics, therapies, service delivery, and public health, with work spanning mental health, reproductive and maternal health, ageing, neurological and cardiovascular diseases, infectious diseases including HIV and respiratory illnesses, and pain and palliative care.

The theme also captures innovations in healthcare access and equity, health workforce development, emergency care, and ambulance services, as well as the ethics and governance of data and clinical decision-making. Research addresses the delivery and reform of healthcare systems and services—from hospital care to community-based provision—and the use of digital technologies, health data, and behavioural science to improve outcomes and efficiency.

Sport, physical activity, and rehabilitation are also important strands, including work on physical and mental wellbeing, injury prevention, and the use of sport to foster inclusion and social change. Research across suicide prevention, substance misuse, and oral health adds further depth, reflecting a broad understanding of health as encompassing both clinical and social dimensions.

Spanning medical, social, policy, and technological research, this theme provides an evidence base for improving health and care systems, promoting population wellbeing, and supporting more inclusive, ethical, and responsive health practices.

This theme covers research driving innovation across engineering, computing, infrastructure, and data systems—often with major implications for industry, the economy, and society. It includes work on robotics, AI, sensors, and smart systems; digital safety and cybersecurity; energy systems and power networks; and telecommunications and satellite infrastructure. Across these domains, research often leads to the development of novel tools, devices, and platforms that enhance performance, safety, and resilience.

Key sectors represented include manufacturing, construction, aerospace, transport, and software development. The theme also includes research into sustainable technologies—from low-carbon infrastructure and electric mobility to waste management and clean energy—and the integration of advanced materials, automation, and green engineering into industrial processes.

A major component of this theme is data-intensive research, including developments in computing architecture, analytics, and high-performance systems, as well as the design of open data standards, digital governance, and knowledge infrastructures. Other contributions focus on occupational and transport safety, emergency preparedness, and the design of secure and ethical digital systems.

Together, this theme reflects a multidisciplinary body of research that combines technical innovation with real-world application, supporting economic productivity, digital transformation, and sustainable development across multiple sectors.

This theme brings together research that addresses the interlinked challenges of environmental change, ecosystem protection, sustainable agriculture, and food systems. It includes work on climate mitigation and adaptation, greenhouse gas emissions, biodiversity conservation, land and marine ecosystem management, pollution, and resource use. Studies span global frameworks and local interventions, often informing environmental regulation, conservation policy, and sustainable land and water practices. Tools such as climate modelling, emissions tracking, and satellite-based monitoring are widely used to support policy and practice.

A significant strand of research focuses on agriculture and food systems—covering crop resilience, pest and disease management, pollination, soil health, animal welfare, and sustainable farming practices. The theme also encompasses the social, ecological, and governance dimensions of food production, access, and dietary sustainability. It includes research on food security, agricultural innovation, and the environmental impacts of different production systems.

Notably, this theme also includes research on tropical diseases, zoonotic infections, and vaccine development—particularly where these intersect with ecological systems, vector control, and global disease surveillance. Work on malaria, viruses, and vaccine strategies appears here due to its links with environmental and ecosystem-based approaches to disease management and prevention.

Overall, the theme integrates insights from environmental science, ecology, agricultural and veterinary research, and aspects of global health to support more sustainable, resilient, and equitable systems for people and nature.

This theme brings together research that explores, preserves, and reimagines cultural expression, heritage, and artistic practice across historical and contemporary contexts. It includes work in the performing and visual arts, literature, music, film, and television, as well as in heritage curation, archaeology, museums, and commemoration. A central focus lies in deepening public understanding, fostering inclusion, and expanding access to cultural and artistic experiences.Research in this theme often engages directly with communities, using creative practice and curatorial innovation to strengthen identity, encourage dialogue, and support wellbeing. Projects have preserved intangible and material heritage, advanced archival and digitisation techniques, and shaped institutional and public approaches to conservation and memory. This includes commemorative practices related to military history, the Holocaust, and contested pasts, often elevating the voices of marginalised or overlooked groups.

The theme also highlights the evolving role of cultural production in public life—from immersive exhibitions and environmental art to theatre, performance, and music-making as tools for education, health, and social change. It encompasses policy-relevant work on cultural access and infrastructure, as well as collaborations that blend artistic and scientific methods to address complex societal issues.

Whether through literature festivals, audiovisual storytelling, historical reconstructions, or new modes of community co-creation, the research represented here underscores the essential role of culture and the arts in building more inclusive, reflective, and resilient societies.

This theme encompasses research that improves access to and experiences of education across the life course, while advancing inclusive practices, linguistic diversity, and equitable participation in learning, culture, and society. It includes studies that shape education policy, teaching and training, curriculum reform, and learning outcomes in schools, universities, and lifelong learning settings. Many projects address inequality in access to education, supporting underrepresented and marginalised learners through innovations in pedagogy, digital learning, and institutional culture.

A strong emphasis is placed on inclusion—particularly in relation to disability, neurodivergence, and social disadvantage. Research supports more accessible educational environments, user-centred design, and practices that reflect the needs and rights of learners, carers, and practitioners. Work on inclusive design and creative practice helps bridge gaps in accessibility and foster wider social engagement.

Language, translation, and literacy are also central to this theme. Studies promote the revitalisation of endangered languages such as Gaelic and Welsh, as well as multilingualism, translation, and language education across diverse communities. Research strengthens cultural identity, global collaboration, and access to literature and learning through linguistic inclusion.

Other case studies focus on the role of education and care in children’s development and wellbeing, science communication and outreach, and the use of arts-based methods for engagement and expression. Social work, safeguarding, and support for families and vulnerable children are also well represented, often linking care, education, and legal reform.

Together, this theme reflects a commitment to education as a space for empowerment, participation, and inclusion—highlighting the diverse ways in which research contributes to fairer, more responsive, and culturally rich systems of learning and support.

This theme brings together research that addresses how societies are governed, how public institutions operate, and how policies can promote fairness, accountability, and resilience in an increasingly complex world. It includes work on law, democracy, economic policy, labour markets, migration, media, international relations, and conflict resolution—spanning both domestic and global contexts.

Researchers in this theme have shaped legislation, strengthened political institutions, and informed public service reform. Their work contributes to more transparent and effective governance, supports the development of responsive legal systems, and enhances the design and evaluation of public policy. Topics such as taxation, welfare, pensions, industrial strategy, and regional development reflect the theme’s strong engagement with core aspects of political economy and state capacity.

Many projects explore the functioning of democratic institutions and the conditions for civic participation, including electoral integrity, freedom of information, and public trust in government. Others address pressing global challenges such as peacebuilding, human rights protection, trade governance, and the regulation of emerging technologies.

Alongside these institutional and policy-oriented contributions, the theme also includes research that informs more inclusive and representative practices. Studies have addressed the experiences and rights of migrants, workers, women, LGBTQ+ people, and religious or ethnic minorities—often shaping law, social care, and public discourse in ways that respond to societal change.

By combining legal, political, economic, and sociocultural perspectives, this theme offers evidence-based insights into how societies manage conflict, deliver justice, support social and economic development, and govern in the public interest.
